news.originalContent:
Photo by Jay L Clendenin/Getty Images

A utility serving rural Northern California wants power rates to climb by more than half as wildfire costs mount under Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Pacific Power, which serves the state’s far northern corner, asked the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) on Nov. 6 to raise its rates by 57 percent beginning Jan. 1, 2027, its application shows. The company’s website says that a 14 percent decrease, which also takes effect Jan. 1, will partially offset the hike.

The company’s filing cites the cost of wildfire work, like trimming trees and strengthening lines, as well as insurance and inflation. Pacific Power told Jefferson Public Radio (JPR) that the change would add about $120 to customers’ bills each month.

“The $120 number does not account for the 14% decrease related to lower than expected power costs,” Simon Gutierrez, a Pacific Power communications representative, said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation.

“Not only is the fire risk extreme, but our service area is very sparsely populated,” Gutierrez told JPR. “It means fewer customers to spread the costs of these investments.”

Pacific Power has about 46,000 California customers, scattered over a service area topping 11,000 square miles in Siskiyou, Del Norte, Modoc and Shasta counties, according to the filing. Gutierrez told JPR that it comes to roughly four customers for each square mile.

The company’s website touts the work it has done since 2022: more than 300 miles of line covered and reinforced, and over 7,000 wooden poles replaced with steel or fiberglass.

In all, Pacific Power is seeking about $103.4 million more, the filing shows. Residential rates would rise 56.9 percent under the request.

Some of the money would pay back wildfire and insurance costs Pacific Power has been running up. The company expects to have about $93.8 million in wildfire mitigation costs and $11.1 million in insurance premiums on its books by the end of 2026 that current rates don’t cover, the filing says. It’s asking to collect that across six years instead of all at once. (RELATED: San Diego Customers Pack Hearings To Fight $270-A-Year Utility Hike)

More than two months have passed since Newsom’s wildfire liability deal with legislative leaders fell through at the end of the session. KQED reported that the Democratic-controlled Assembly never took a vote on it.

Newsom’s first version would have moved more of the wildfire risk from utilities onto home insurers, KQED reported. Part of the plan would have stopped insurers from suing to recoup what they paid fire victims. Insurers, attorneys and fire-victim groups fought that plan as a utility bailout, and Democratic lawmakers rebuffed it, the outlet reported.

Newsom had signaled that the deal did not go far enough. In an Aug. 29 statement after it was announced, he said that “this system needs full structural reform — not a partial one.”

He called on lawmakers to come back next year and “finish the work we started,” including efforts to “stabilize electricity rates.”

“The communities we serve in California are facing some of the highest fire risk in the country. These are critical upgrades needed to protect these communities,” Gutierrez said in his statement. “The costs of the materials needed to make these investments have gone up dramatically.”

On Sept. 1, Newsom asked the CPUC to report on what the state’s failure to pass structural wildfire reforms is doing to utilities. The commission’s Nov. 1 report warned that wildfire costs “will continue to increase utility bills” if nothing changes.

“Without reform, even this status quo is likely unsustainable,” the commission wrote.

The report found that at the state’s three biggest investor-owned utilities, wildfire costs make up roughly 10 percent to 14 percent of a typical household’s bill. Inland Pacific Gas and Electric customers have it worst, at 29 percent of the average bill. Along the coast it is 16 percent.

Utilities have spent “further tens of billions of dollars” on mitigation work the state requires, and those costs will be passed along to ratepayers, the report noted.

Newsom signed the 2019 law that created California’s wildfire fund, which was set up with about $21 billion to pay claims. Ratepayers are paying for $10.5 billion of it through a charge on their bills, the CPUC report shows.

Newsom also signed Senate Bill 254 in 2025, which created a second account that could pay up to $18 billion more in claims but holds no money yet. Customers could end up paying up to $9 billion of that from 2036 to 2045, the report said, but only if the fund needs it and the CPUC signs off.

Pacific Power is not part of the fund. The report noted that PacifiCorp, the company that does business as Pacific Power, is one of the utilities that “do not have access to the Wildfire Fund under existing State law.” (RELATED: Newsom Reportedly Devising Plan To Saddle Ratepayers With Wildfire Cleanup Fees)

“I just signed into law the biggest electricity bill refunds in a decade — up to $60 billion to help bring down costs for California families,” Newsom said in a Sept. 19, 2025, press release announcing the package.

Californians paid an average of 32.58 cents per kilowatt-hour for residential power from January through August, Energy Information Administration figures show. That was the second-highest rate in the country after Hawaii and well above the national average of 18.19 cents.

Edward Ring, director of water and energy policy at the California Policy Center, said in a statement to the DCNF that state policy shapes most of what Pacific Gas and Electric customers pay. Working from what he called a typical rate of 35 cents per kilowatt-hour for the utility, he estimated that changing those policies could eventually bring it down to about 21 cents.

“In the meantime, it was the state that was most negligent,” Ring said. “They forced the utilities to (1) purchase more expensive renewable electricity, (2) still keep their lines clear of flammable material, and (3) keep their rates to the consumer down. That was an impossible request.”

Jason Isaac, CEO of the American Energy Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF that Democrats serious about affordability should back more nuclear power, natural gas and coal.

“Americans need more dependable electricity and fewer government obstacles driving up the price,” Isaac said.

PacifiCorp also agreed in February to a $575 million settlement of federal claims tied to six fires in California and Oregon, including the 2020 Slater Fire and the 2022 McKinney Fire in California, the Justice Department announced. The department noted that the claims were “allegations only,” and PacifiCorp still denies liability.

In Oregon, an appeals court in April reversed and remanded a class-action judgment against PacifiCorp, the CPUC report says. The state’s highest court took up the case and heard arguments Nov. 3, Oregon Public Broadcasting reported.

Jurors had found PacifiCorp grossly negligent in 2023 for starting four fires over Labor Day weekend in 2020, the outlet reported. The court will decide what happens to the more than $1 billion that about 200 survivors have been awarded so far. Its ruling could also determine whether about 2,000 more claims get considered.

S&P Global Ratings cut PacifiCorp’s credit rating three times between June 2023 and November 2025, citing wildfire litigation among its reasons, the CPUC report says. The agency then put the company on watch for a further downgrade in March. After the April appeals ruling, S&P revised its outlook on PacifiCorp to positive. PacifiCorp had put its probable wildfire losses at about $2.85 billion as of June 30, settlements included, the report noted.

PacifiCorp is now rated one notch above junk, its filing says. Under current rates, the company says it would earn a negative 2.636 percent return on equity in California.

Pacific Power has not always gotten what it wanted from regulators. When it sought a 25.7 percent overall increase in 2022, the CPUC approved roughly 17.5 percent in December 2023.

“We understand the magnitude of this request,” Gutierrez said in his statement. “This filing is the beginning of a process, and we welcome a review and discussion about what the right balance is between wildfire investments and rates for our California customers.”

The company wants the rates to take effect Jan. 1, 2027, but its website notes that the CPUC’s review may last several months.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

Marco Rubio reached back more than 2,000 years to a Roman general to warn the International Criminal Court (ICC) that its rulings carry no force over Americans.

The secretary of state delivered the message during a keynote to the Federalist Society’s National Lawyers Convention in Washington Friday, according to a State Department transcript.

The same answer the Roman commander Pompey once gave to those citing their city’s charters against his legions would greet any move to enforce the court’s decrees on U.S. citizens, Rubio stated. “Stop quoting laws to men with swords,” he said. The line drew laughter, and he joked that the words were not politically correct.

FULL REMARKS: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Delivers Keynote Address, Answers Questions at Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention https://t.co/I9Zbat5ZVY

Rubio accused the court and its global-bureaucracy allies of making themselves “judge and jury and executioner of the international order” while answering to no one, according to the transcript. The tribunal now claims the power to investigate, prosecute and jail Americans under rules the country never approved, he stated. (RELATED: Trump Admin Announces Sanctions Against International Criminal Court Chief)

The secretary cast international law itself as a weapon of a global elite, arguing that critics had wielded it against nearly every major foreign policy decision of the Trump administration, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported. He pointed to the U.S. military’s strikes on cartel boats in the Caribbean and the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro as moves that drew such objections, and he turned the same scorn on the United Nations.

The address was Rubio’s first major speech at home since Republicans absorbed heavy losses in this month’s midterm elections, and the crowd met him with a standing ovation, AFP reported. His choice of a prominent legal audience fed new speculation about a 2028 presidential bid, according to the Hill.

The appearance followed the sweeping sanctions the administration placed on the court in October as part of a campaign it says will dismantle the tribunal, the Associated Press (AP) reported. Washington signed the treaty that created the ICC yet never ratified it, which leaves the United States outside the court alongside Israel, Russia and China, AFP reported.

Enforcement is where the court runs thin, since it fields no police force and leans on member nations to arrest anyone it indicts, AP reported. The United States is not one of them.

Rubio tied the fight to national identity in closing. “To submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats would be to betray who we are, to betray ourselves,” he stated in the remarks.

(عکس از رابرتو اشمیت / خبرگزاری فرانسه از طریق گتی ایماژ)
مارکو روبیو بیش از 2000 سال پیش به یک ژنرال رومی مراجعه کرد تا به دادگاه کیفری بین‌المللی (ICC) هشدار دهد که احکام آن هیچ قدرتی بر آمریکایی‌ها ندارد. بر اساس رونوشت وزارت امور خارجه، وزیر امور خارجه این پیام را در جریان سخنرانی اصلی کنوانسیون ملی وکلای جامعه فدرالیست در روز جمعه در واشنگتن ارائه کرد. روبیو اظهار داشت که همان پاسخی که پومپیوس فرمانده رومی زمانی به کسانی که به منشورهای شهرشان علیه لژیون‌هایش استناد می‌کردند، از هر حرکتی برای اجرای احکام دادگاه در مورد شهروندان ایالات متحده استقبال می‌کرد. او گفت: «از ذکر قوانین برای مردان شمشیردار خودداری کنید. این خط باعث خنده شد و او به شوخی گفت که این کلمات از نظر سیاسی درست نیستند. اظهارات کامل: مارکو روبیو، وزیر امور خارجه، سخنرانی کلیدی، پاسخ به سؤالات در کنوانسیون ملی وکلای جامعه فدرالیست https://t.co/I9Zbat5ZVY
روبیو دادگاه و متحدان بوروکراسی جهانی آن را متهم کرد که خود را «قاضی، هیئت منصفه و مجری نظم بین‌الملل» می‌دانند در حالی که بر اساس متن به هیچ‌کس پاسخ نمی‌دادند. او گفت که دادگاه اکنون ادعا می کند که این قدرت را دارد که آمریکایی ها را تحت قوانینی که هرگز تأیید نکرده است، تحقیق، محاکمه و زندانی کند. (مرتبط: ادمین ترامپ علیه رئیس دیوان کیفری بین المللی تحریم ها را اعلام کرد)

news.originalContent:
At least 11 employees at two of America’s most powerful intelligence and cyber warfare agencies have died by suicide over the past year, prompting scrutiny from Congress and the White House.

The deaths occurred among military personnel, civilian employees and contractors working for the National Security Agency (NSA) and U.S. Cyber Command, including five suicides within roughly one month that military officials classified as a suicide cluster, according to The Japan Times. The deaths have prompted congressional inquiries and new restrictions on working hours as the agencies grapple with mounting operational demands from overseas conflicts, although officials have not determined that workplace pressures caused the suicides.

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.
news.content: ارتش اسرائیل به حملات شبانه در جنوب لبنان از جمله در روستای کفرمان پرداخت و گفت که این حملات بعد از ظهر دوشنبه پس از پرتاب دو پهپاد انفجاری توسط تروریست‌های حزب‌الله به سمت نیروهای اسرائیلی در خط الراس علی طاهر در جنوب لبنان آغاز شد. هیچ نیروی ارتش اسرائیل در پرتاب هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین آسیبی ندید و ارتش اعلام کرد که بلافاصله حمله به زیرساخت‌های حزب‌الله را در چندین منطقه در جنوب لبنان از جمله تأسیسات ذخیره‌سازی سلاح آغاز کرده است.   هیچ نیروی ارتش اسرائیل در پرتاب هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین آسیبی ندید و ارتش اعلام کرد که بلافاصله حمله به زیرساخت‌های حزب‌الله را در چندین منطقه در جنوب لبنان از جمله تأسیسات ذخیره‌سازی سلاح آغاز کرده است. خودرویی که در آن دو نفر کشته شدند. آسوشیتدپرس گزارش داد که این خودرو متعلق به انجمن پیشاهنگی و نجات لبنان، الرساله است و یکی از کشته شدگان، امدادگر این سازمان است. دو نفر دیگر زخمی شدند. همزمان، گزارش‌های لبنانی حاکی از آن است که ساختمانی در کفارمان که تعداد زیادی از مردم در آن اقامت داشتند نیز مورد اصابت قرار گرفت و 9 نفر از جمله زن و کودک کشته و 11 نفر زخمی شدند.   ارتش اسرائیل در پاسخ گفت: قبل از حملات، اقداماتی برای کاهش آسیب به افراد غیرمجاز از جمله استفاده از مهمات دقیق و نظارت هوایی انجام شد. این ادعا که در نتیجه این اعتصابات به چندین نفر آسیب وارد شده است، در حال بررسی است. ارتش اسرائیل گفت که علاوه بر این، دنبال کنید

According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.
